gyrA.cellular_role: Type II DNA Topoisomerase relieving supercoiling during replication
gyrA.mechanism_of_resistance: Point mutation alters Ser83/Asp87, destroying water-metal ion bridge coordinating quinolone pharmacophore

parC.cellular_role: Decatenation of daughter chromosomes during cell division
parC.mechanism_of_resistance: Point mutation (Ser80Ile) synergizes with gyrA to cause high-level fluoroquinolone refractoriness

blaNDM.active_site_target: Bimetallic Zn1/Zn2 active site bridging hydroxide
blaNDM.mechanism_of_resistance: Hydrolyzes all beta-lactams including carbapenems, cephalosporins, and penicillins (except monobactam aztreonam)

blaCTX.active_site_target: Ser70 catalytic active site with flexible omega loop
blaCTX.mechanism_of_resistance: Preferentially hydrolyzes oxyimino-cephalosporins (Cefotaxime, Ceftriaxone, Ceftazidime) and penicillins

blaOXA.mechanism_of_resistance: Hydrolyzes penicillins and carbapenems; poorly inhibited by clavulanic acid

blaKPC.active_site_target: Deep active site accommodating carbapenem 6-alpha hydroxyethyl group
blaKPC.mechanism_of_resistance: Hydrolyzes all penicillins, cephalosporins, and carbapenems

ampC.mechanism_of_resistance: Constitutive or derepressed hydrolysis of broad-spectrum cephalosporins and penicillins

ompK36.cellular_role: Hydrophilic solute passive diffusion channel (size cutoff ~600 Da)
ompK36.mechanism_of_resistance: Porin mutation / deletion restricts entry of carbapenems into the periplasm, synergizing with beta-lactamases

mcr.mechanism_of_resistance: Adds phosphoethanolamine to Lipid A, neutralizing negative surface charge and preventing cationic polymyxin binding

mecA.mechanism_of_resistance: Low binding affinity for beta-lactams allows peptidoglycan crosslinking despite high drug concentrations (MRSA phenotype)

vanA.mechanism_of_resistance: Replaces terminal D-Ala-D-Ala with D-Ala-D-Lac, reducing glycopeptide binding affinity 1000-fold (VRE / VRSA)

rpoB.mechanism_of_resistance: Ser450Leu point mutation causes steric clash in the rifamycin-binding pocket, preventing transcription blockade

katG.cellular_role: Oxidative stress defense and pro-drug activator
katG.mechanism_of_resistance: Impaired catalytic activation of isoniazid prodrug into isonicotinoyl-NAD adduct, conferring high-level INH resistance

embB.cellular_role: Arabinogalactan and lipoarabinomannan cell wall synthesis
embB.mechanism_of_resistance: Steric hindrance prevents ethambutol binding to the arabinosyltransferase catalytic cleft

tetM.cellular_role: GTPase releasing tetracyclines from ribosomal A-site
tetM.mechanism_of_resistance: Allosterically alters ribosomal decoding site, dislodging tetracyclines without altering 16S sequence

armA.mechanism_of_resistance: Methylates G1405 in the 16S rRNA A-site, creating steric block against 4,6-disubstituted 2-deoxystreptamine aminoglycosides

ermB.mechanism_of_resistance: Dimethylates A2058 in the 23S rRNA exit tunnel, blocking macrolide and lincosamide binding (MLSB phenotype)

blaZ.mechanism_of_resistance: Rapidly hydrolyzes unprotected penicillins (Amoxicillin, Ampicillin, Penicillin G); requires beta-lactamase inhibitor (Clavulanic acid, Tazobactam) or penicillinase-stable isoxazolyl penicillin

vanB.mechanism_of_resistance: Replaces terminal D-Ala-D-Ala with D-Ala-D-Lac upon vancomycin induction (retains susceptibility to teicoplanin)

ompK35.cellular_role: Hydrophilic solute passive diffusion channel (size cutoff ~600 Da)
ompK35.mechanism_of_resistance: Porin down-regulation or loss restricts entry of cephalosporins and carbapenems into the periplasm

oprD.cellular_role: Basic amino acid and carbapenem specific entry channel
oprD.mechanism_of_resistance: Mutational loss or down-regulation of OprD causes selective carbapenem (Meropenem/Imipenem) impermeability in P. aeruginosa

grlA.mechanism_of_resistance: Primary target mutation for fluoroquinolones in S. aureus (Ser80Phe/Tyr)

inhA.cellular_role: Mycolic acid fatty acid elongation (FAS-II system)
inhA.active_site_target: Promoter region (-15 C->T mutation) causing InhA target overexpression
inhA.mechanism_of_resistance: InhA promoter mutation causes low-level isoniazid and ethionamide cross-resistance in M. tuberculosis
